record.field: Backup operations — Borg to disk (LXD hosts → tull1) and Restic to S3 (Garage buckets). Per-artifact archives, Dirvish-compatible retention (hist + EXPIRES + Never-pinning), restore, and drift diagnosis.
backup, borg, restic, garage, s3, bucket, archive, snapshot, retention, prune, restore, återställ, pin, dirvish, lxd-backup, backup-status, stale

# Backup Operations — Borg (disk) + Restic (S3)
Vertel has **two** backup systems. They do different jobs — never mix them up:
| System | Target | What it backs up | |---|---|---| | **Borg** | **Disk** — `tull1:/srv/borgbackup` (XFS, prjquota, 6.3 TB) | LXD hosts: per-artifact (containers, VMs, snapshots, custom volumes, buckets, LXD-db) + host-level `/etc`+`/srv` | | **Restic** | **S3** — Garage buckets | Customer Garage buckets → `<customer>-backup` |
**Dirvish is RETIRED** (`dirvish/retire.sls`, 2026-09-25). It survives only as the old vaults on `dirvishtull0`/`dirvishtull1` and as the migration source. Do not propose Dirvish for new backups.
## Borg — architecture
``` fors ──lxd-backup.sh──► ssh://root@62.109.49.47/srv/borgbackup/lxd/fors tull0 ──lxd-backup.sh──► ssh://root@192.168.11.30/srv/borgbackup/lxd/tull0 strand ──lxd-backup.sh──► ssh://root@192.168.11.30/srv/borgbackup/lxd/strand └─ tull1:/srv/borgbackup ```
The job runs **locally on each LXD host** (discovery reads LXD's local config); only the write goes over SSH to tull1. tull1 owns the disk.
**One borg archive per artifact per night** — that is the whole point: you can restore ONE container without touching the others. Archive naming: `<host>-<kind>-<name>-<YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS>`.
Cron (all three hosts):
``` 0 1 * * * lxd-backup.sh # nightly per-artifact backup 0 2 * * 0 lxd-backup-prune.sh --dry-run 0 3 * * 0 lxd-backup-prune.sh # retention 0 6 * * * lxd-backup-status.sh 30 2 * * * borg-backup.sh # host-level (complement) ```
## Retention — Dirvish semantics preserved
| Dirvish | Borg | |---|---| | `default.hist` | `/etc/lxd-backup/hist/<prefix>.hist` | | `expire-default: +15 days` | `borg prune --keep-within 15d` | | `EXPIRES: Never` | archive excluded from the prune glob (pinned) | | `dirvish-expire` | `borg prune --glob-archives` | | `dirvish-expire --dry-run` | `--dry-run` |
`borg prune` has NO "keep this archive" flag — a pinned archive is protected by never being in the glob passed to prune, then verified to still exist (exit 3 if it vanished).
## The tools
- **borg_status** — per-artifact health (status ok/warning/error, stale count, age_hours). START HERE. - **borg_artifacts** — what discovery WOULD find (no backup run). - **borg_list** — archives in a repo, filter by prefix → "which restore points exist?" - **borg_backup_run** — run a backup now (destructive). - **borg_prune** — retention; `dry_run=true` is safe. - **borg_pin** — pin/unpin (EXPIRES=Never). - **borg_restore** — extract ONE artifact to a directory (destructive). - **restic_status** — per-customer Garage bucket status. - **restic_restore_list** — restore points for a customer. - **restic_restore** — restore a customer bucket; `dry_run=true` is safe.
## Diagnosis pattern
1. **borg_status** on the host → is the newest archive fresh, or stale? 2. Stale/missing artifact? → **borg_artifacts** (is it discovered at all?) 3. Discovery OK but no archive? → check `/var/log/lxd-backup/backup.log` 4. Repo questions → **borg_list** with the artifact prefix 5. Restic/S3 questions → **restic_status** on the `restic` minion
## Restore
**Borg** — per artifact (extracts to a *directory*, does NOT replace the container):
``` borg_restore(minion="fors", artifact="containers/sparv", target="/tmp/restore-sparv") ``` Then, to actually restore: stop/delete the container in LXD, move rootfs back to the pool path, `lxc start`. Those last steps are manual on purpose.
**Restic** — always run ON the restic minion (192.168.11.112), where `/etc/rclone/<customer>.conf` and the restic password live:
``` restic_restore_list(customer="dina") # which dates? restic_restore(customer="dina", dry_run=True) # look, write nothing ```
## Pitfalls (verified in production)
- **`borg repo-list` does not exist in borg 1.2.8** — use `borg list`. - **`BORG_PASSCOMMAND` ≠ `LXD_BACKUP_PASSCOMMAND`** — borg only reads `BORG_*`. Without it every cron run fails on an interactive prompt. - **`borg list --format` writes NO newlines in 1.2.8** — add `{NEWLINE}` explicitly, otherwise `wc -l` reports 1 and status reports go silently empty. - **`lxc storage get <pool> source` returns EMPTY** on fors/tull0 — LXD only exposes `source` with `--target <server_name>` (from `lxc query /1.0`, NOT `hostname`). - **`BORG_RELOCATED_REPO_ACCESS_IS_OK=yes`** is required when a repo has moved hosts. - **`msgpack` conflict** — a pip msgpack shadows the apt version borg needs. - **Never auto-start a restore into a live container.** Extract to a directory first.
## Publishing
`lxd_backup/publish.sls` runs **on the Salt master** (cron 06:40) and POSTs to the **shared** `/saltstack/log` webhook with `source=lxd-backup`. The webhook is shared with dirvish/restic/odoosa/clicktest/wazuh — the contract (URL, Bearer, field names) must never change; only add new sources.
